---
title: Report what you did
---

## Reporting standards

Use GUILD and RECORD guidance to describe data sources, identifiers, blocking, comparison, decision rules, quality checks, and any clerical review.

## What to document

- data custodians and legal basis
- source population and date coverage
- identifiers used, transformed, or excluded
- blocking passes and comparison fields
- thresholds, review rules, and final match counts
- how linkage error was assessed and discussed

::: {.callout-note .reporting}
## Reporting note

A reviewer should be able to understand the linkage design, its limits, and its likely effect on estimates without reverse-engineering code.
:::

## Privacy and governance

Linkage design should respect the separation principle wherever possible. Privacy-preserving linkage methods can reduce direct exposure to identifiers, but they still need clear evaluation and governance.
